Component reservations require the caller effort-3 envelope and are cumulative conservative bounds, not allocator measurements. They can reject work whose actual peak allocation would fit.
Algorithm checkpoints bound changed loop work; allocator/COW/runtime copies and scheduling have no real-time cancellation guarantee.
Timing comparisons exercise serial internal encodes without an operation-budget context. The separate budget probe covers one, two and eight workers, not concurrent steady-state telemetry.
Process peak RSS is process-wide; allocation counts, copy-byte telemetry, peak algorithm workspace and widest profile/precision/corpus coverage remain open.
Local Swift 6.4 macOS arm64 evidence does not qualify hosted Swift 6.2, both Linux architectures or minimum-OS/device runtime.

performanceGate.status: Open; no stable-release acceptance or baseline waiver.
performanceGate.reason: Higher-effort safety checks and bounded stable sorting add work. The initial implementation reproduced roughly 8-11 percent tree-case overhead. Moving checks outside tight radix and learner blocks reduced the measured cost; remaining cost is explicitly retained for review, not silently waived. Activity-gray process RSS also rises about 5.5 percent in both runs; the stable merge uses an admitted full-length scratch array, but allocator-level attribution is not established.
performanceGate.scope: Internal effort-8/9 median latency and effort-7 activity-gray process RSS exceed the repeated 5-percent threshold; public effort-3 control has no repeated regression.
